subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: Should shared auth-profile refresh automatically retry transient provider/network failures, and which error classes and total time budget are allowed?
rationale: The code has no canonical cross-provider retry contract, and the choice affects built-in providers plus plugin refresh hooks, rotating credentials, lock duration, and user-visible auth failure timing.

options.title: Retry classified transient failures
options.body: Retry a bounded set such as network errors, timeouts, 5xx, and explicitly supported rate limits while excluding terminal OAuth and malformed-success failures.

options.title: Keep single-shot refresh
options.body: Preserve the current contract and rely on credential adoption, provider-specific behavior, and a later agent request or gateway restart for recovery.

options.title: Make retries provider-owned
options.body: Require each provider or plugin refresh implementation to declare and implement its own retry policy instead of applying a shared manager rule.

recommendation.title: Retry classified transient failures
recommendation.body: Retry a bounded set such as network errors, timeouts, 5xx, and explicitly supported rate limits while excluding terminal OAuth and malformed-success failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The centralized OAuth lifecycle manager and its owner boundary originate in this contributor's refactor.
